findings.summary: Definition-only symbol existence refuses standard-library and external methods, macros, attributes and lints that the workspace calls.
findings.evidence: Shape (a) makes any bare snake_case word of 5+ characters in a `Code survey:` a candidate. Decision 4 counts it as existing only if a line-start `fn`/`struct`/field/variant defines it, a `use` or `extern crate` line names it, or a Cargo.toml lists it as a crate. Words such as `and_then`, `unwrap_or_default`, `filter_map`, `into_iter`, `assert_eq!`, `include_str!`, `skip_serializing_if`, `deny_unknown_fields`, `must_use` and `too_many_arguments` are called or used in the workspace but never defined or imported, so they would be refused. The plan itself uses this vocabulary (Decision 1: "chain it with `.and_then`"). The Open questions name only unimported prelude types. The reader gets one correction, so each false refusal is costly. Fix: Count a symbol as existing when it appears as a whole word on any non-comment code line of a .rs file in the snapshot. Skip lines starting `//`, doc lines included; string literals may optionally be skipped. That covers call sites, macro uses, attributes and lint names. Names from unlanded jobs are neither defined nor called in the snapshot, so they are still refused. Alternatively, add `.name(`, `name!` and `#[...]` occurrences to the scope collector. Add guard tests for `and_then`, `assert_eq` and a serde attribute name.
findings.location: Plan Decision 4 (symbol existence = definitions + use-statement names + crate names); Decision 3 shape (a) bare snake_case

findings.summary: The hyphenated-stem trigger matches ordinary English compounds.
findings.evidence: Design-doc stems in this repository are compounds such as records-history, defaults-loop and ci-routing. An earlier job's unlanded create such as docs/design~-cause.md would trigger on any reading that writes 'root-cause' in prose. That forces a boilerplate out_of_scope entry and spends the one correction. Fix: Trigger on a hyphenated stem only when it is in backticks or written with its extension, or trigger only on snake_case stems and full paths. Keep the criterion-2 role case by backticking `context-engineer` in its fixture. Add a guard test: a prose 'root-cause' does not trigger an unlanded root-cause.md.
findings.location: Plan Decision 2 (stem trigger: 5+ characters with `_` or `-`)

findings.summary: The 'new' clause window breaks at dots and colons inside code tokens.
findings.evidence: The window scans back only to the previous `.`, `;`, `:` or newline. Surveys contain `reading.rs`, `foo.bar()`, `Athena::ask` and `reading.rs:2600`, so a clause is cut in the middle of a code token. Fix: Treat `.` as a boundary only when whitespace or the end of the text follows it, and never treat `::` as a boundary. Add tests with 'adds to reading.rs a new function `x`' and with a `::` path inside the clause.

findings.summary: The import and crate-name rule may read as conflicting with the reading's out_of_scope line.
findings.evidence: The reading puts 'Symbol-shape matching beyond definitions found in .rs files' out of scope. The plan also counts `use` names, Cargo crate names and std/core/alloc paths as existing. Fix: State in D146 and the doc comment that this only widens what counts as existing (fewer refusals), that it is not new shape matching, and why it is needed.
findings.location: Plan Decision 4 vs the reading's Out of scope

findings.summary: Part 1 refuses fixture or historical paths named in criteria or assumptions.
findings.evidence: Criteria that describe test fixtures (for example, naming crates/athena-core/src/code_health.rs as a refused example) or past removals name paths absent from the snapshot. The plan's own Criterion 2 fixtures have this shape. Fix: Name the out_of_scope repair for fixture and historical paths in the error message and in D146. Add a test in which a criterion names a fixture path, an out_of_scope entry names it, and the reading is accepted.

summary: I read read_once (reading.rs 372-539), referenced_jobs (2335; MAX_REFERENCED_JOBS is 3), check_prior_result_and_scope, the EarlierAttempt fields in athena-context briefs.rs, and Git::ls_tree and cat_blobs in athena-git. The functions, helpers and line numbers the plan names exist. The wiring point at reading.rs:520 is where the fault starts. The reading-named job loader also covers cited jobs past the cap of 3. The demonstrations name real seams: pure-function arguments, and Athena::ask through the fake reader. Each would fail without the behavior. Criterion 6 is honestly stated as a hand-built table plus fixtures, because no stored readings exist. One soundness problem needs revision before code. Part 2 treats any bare snake_case survey word as a symbol, but counts it as existing only if it is defined, imported with `use`, or a crate name. So standard-library and external methods, macros, attributes and lints the workspace calls (and_then, assert_eq!, skip_serializing_if, too_many_arguments) would be refused. The plan's own prose uses this vocabulary. The simpler, more correct rule is any whole-word occurrence on a non-comment .rs code line, which still refuses names from unlanded jobs. Smaller issues: hyphenated stems can match English compounds, the 'new' clause window breaks at `.rs` and `::`, the import/crate-name widening should be reconciled in writing with the out-of-scope line, and fixture and historical paths in criteria need a documented repair.
